provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 82-84; antecedent 1862 text-layer lines 20401-20418; 1922 Mame printed p. 83, artifact PDF p. 197
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the 1962 prints the conclusion written out (5 words); the public-domain witnesses abbreviate it to the short cue; 1862 text layer damages 3 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: salutaris noster et ut -> salut ris uoster etut; quadragesimale -> quadragesimaie; mentes nostras celestibus instrue disciplinis -> men digitized by google feria ii post dominicam i quadragesihmb h tes uostras; 1922 Mame text layer damages 1 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): conuerte -> onuerte; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 83, artifact PDF p. 197; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 27032 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Feria II post dominicam I in Quadragesima) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Oratio the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. The 1862's own locus for this day scores only 0.44 on a token-level alignment; every difference behind that score is recogniser damage (accents dropped, words split at line breaks, running heads and the scan's watermark intruding), not a different petition. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster: et, ut nobis jejunium quadragesimale
proficiat, mentes nostras caelestibus instrue disciplinis. Per Dominum
nostrum Jesum Christum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Salutaris tui, Domine, munere satiati supplices exoramus: ut, cujus laetamur
gustu, renovemur effectu. Per Dominum nostrum.
